QF.id: AIFM CIII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_31

question.text: The Dissolution Period of a Cat III AIF scheme:

answer.text: Can be extended indefinitely upon investor consent
Shall not be more than the original tenure of the scheme, and cannot be extended after expiry
Is permitted only if SEBI individually approves each case

explanation.text: The Logic: The Dissolution Period shall not be more than the original tenure of the scheme and cannot be extended after its expiry. A merchant-banker filing (Information Memorandum plus Due-Diligence Certificate) must be made before the Liquidation Period expires. Fresh commitments and new investments are barred during the Dissolution Period. The Trap: Indefinite extension (A) contradicts the rule. A fixed 2-year cap (C) is not the rule — the cap is the original scheme tenure. SEBI per-case approval (D) misreads the merchant-banker filing process. Note: The Dissolution-Period cap (original tenure; no post-expiry extension) is set out in the workbook on p. 359.
